body.heading: Waiting to feel ready
paragraphs: The common picture of motivation is a spark that arrives first and makes work easy. In practice, for most people and most tasks, the order runs the other way: a small action comes first, and the feeling of motivation trails behind it.
Think of the last time you did not want to go for a walk or start an assignment, but felt better five minutes in. The feeling was produced by the doing, not required before it.

body.heading: Start embarrassingly small
paragraphs: Use that order deliberately. When motivation is missing, shrink the first action until it is almost laughable: open the document, put on the shoes, write one sentence. Tiny starts bypass the argument in your head.
This is not a trick that works every time — tiredness, illness and genuinely hard seasons are real. But on an ordinary unmotivated day, action first is the most reliable lever you have.

takeaway: Do not wait to feel like it. Start tiny, and let the feeling catch up.
